finding: Startup read its route before owner adoption, cleared recovery-yield state before adoption/worker admission and retired an old worker separately from publication, without a final route/current-worker check. A delayed startup could overwrite intervening route/worker/yield authority.
change: Read-only early route/yield refusal remains; adopted owner supplies the authoritative route/epoch. One unscheduled commit checks route, owner/adopted state, feature/movement/Zeus/external gates, current brain and exact observed yield. It validates supported vehicle availability before retirement, rechecks resulting authority after cleanup, then clears only the observed yield and publishes a new generation/brain/handle. Same live route returns the existing worker; terminal/exhausted same-route work remains refused. Seat-only remote-vehicle casualty support remains unchanged.

validation.fixture: Normal traffic following must first physically approach, then duplicate startup must preserve the genuine live brain/handle and nonterminal state. PREPARED_NOT_RUN. No worker/state/cap injection.

limits: Locality adoption itself is a separate boundary and may legitimately change current state; route capture follows it.
Cleanup can end the old worker even if a resulting authority change refuses the new one; no rollback is claimed.
No physical native event timing, actual-provider HC migration, repeatability or one-time cleanup cost acceptance.
Whole HBQ parity, native bilateral queue clearing and all65-family acceptance remain open.
